title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 9
text: “So, this is his family home, huh…”

Following the directions I’d been given, I arrived at a farm that appeared to be the Robin Hood-like figure’s family home. But… what is this? I felt like the character of the surrounding trees was slightly different. While there were indeed trees like chocolate trees, there were also mysterious fields and what looked like a workshop. I could tell at a glance that the atmosphere here was different from that of the town.
Why is lightning flashing across the sky? And the clouds look ominous.
“It’s kind of creepy, isn’t it?”
“Yeah, you’re right.”
I cautiously got out of the carriage and knocked on the door of a house near the farm.
“Hello?”

I heard a girl’s voice. With a clatter, a girl who looked to be about fifteen came out. At first glance, she seemed like an ordinary girl. A little on the chubby side, though. Well, I guess you’d gain weight living in a place this sugary. She’s probably eating chocolate every day.
“Who are you?”
“Oh, I’m… someone sent by this guy.”
With that, I handed the girl the letter of introduction I’d received from the Robin Hood. As soon as she read it, she started trembling uncontrollably.
“Mom! A letter from my big brother! And it’s definitely the Shield Hero!”

After bowing, the girl dashed back inside the house. I’d been sending money to the Robin Hood in exchange for his services… and we’d been exchanging letters, so I figured they’d recognize me right away. With panic written all over their faces, the Robin Hood’s sister and mother came out to greet us.
“Well, well, what a pleasure to see you, Shield Hero!”

The mother was a bit on the plump side, but she had the look of a healthy, down-to-earth country woman. She’d probably look good in a traditional apron, but she was wearing work clothes instead. I wonder if they’re harvesting chocolate or something?

Just like the Robin Hood’s sister, she seemed pretty ordinary—quite different from her appearance. She gave off the vibe of a run-of-the-mill chocolate farmer. …Though I don’t actually know if chocolate farmers are that common.
“So… what brings you here? Are you here to buy some chocolate?”
“Ah, I’d like to place a large order.”
“Well, well—this entrance hall just won’t do. Please come inside.”
“Uh…”

I don’t really care where we do this, as long as we can get down to business. I’ll discuss things like how much I can order and the price per kilogram, though. I beckoned to Raphtalia and went inside the Robin Hood’s family home.
“This is our village’s specialty chocolate drink! Please, help yourself!”
“That looks like the kind of drink that’d actually make my throat even drier.”
We have them in my world too, but chocolate drinks are pretty rough, aren’t they? I can’t imagine wanting to drink that thick, brown liquid.
“Please also try some of our homemade cake!”

For some reason, a fluorescent pink cake appears. And it’s even slightly warm. They definitely whipped this up in a hurry. You see cakes like this overseas, but even I’m hesitant to reach for it. That said, I can’t just leave it untouched. We’re about to negotiate, after all. With that in mind, I take another look at the cake.
What the heck is this? What a gross-looking cake. Ugh… it looks like the color changes with temperature. What kind of gourmet manga did this cake come from?!
Every once in a while, you come across bizarre dishes like this in this world. I wouldn’t dream of trying to recreate it. Even if people say it tastes good, I don’t want to eat it.
“Is there some reason it’s fluorescent pink?”
“Huh? We’re using high-quality chocolate from the village, though…”
“I think you’d be better off not putting that on the market.”
Wanting chocolate in a color like this must be the result of a unique set of values taking hold in an environment where chocolate is readily available.
“Um…”
“Don’t be so nervous. I’m here for business. Just treat me like you normally would.”

I appreciate the discount because I’m the Hero, but my goal isn’t to exploit them. If they do things that make sense, I’ll make concessions. I’m not a monster, after all. There are times when I negotiate deals so that both sides come out ahead.
“Do you want some, Raphtalia?”
“Um… I’ll have some.”

Oh? She’s brave. Raphtalia is eating the cake and saying it’s delicious. Does it taste good despite its appearance? No matter how you look at it, she’s the type who gets judged unfairly based on her looks. The Robin Hood’s sister also relaxed a bit at Raphtalia’s reaction.
“Well, a little small talk is fine, but…”
“Right. Let’s get down to business. How much chocolate are you looking for?”
“It doesn’t have to come exclusively from here, but—”
With that, I stated the amount of chocolate I’d likely need for the event. Of course, that included what we’d use for practice and other things as well.
“I’m not sure if our farm alone can cover that much…”
“That’s fine. The real question is, how much per kilo will you sell it for? Don’t try to butter me up, okay?”
“Well…”

The Robin Hood’s mother continued our conversation with the eye of a businesswoman. It’s fine to haggle, but it’s also important not to cause the other party a massive loss. After all, even if I buy it at rock-bottom prices here, what about next year? I could buy from another farm, but there’s a chance bad rumors might spread. If that happens, no one will actually want to sell me chocolate anymore.

If this had happened before that battle, things would have been different. Back then, I intended to return to the real world eventually. Even if some bad rumors got out, it wouldn’t have been a problem since I was going back in the end. But now that I plan to stay in this world for the rest of my life, I need to consider those kinds of things as well.

Besides, while it’s fine to be brazen, I’m not so ungrateful as to ruin the Righteous Thief’s family home. The Righteous Thief is, after all, under my command—in fact, I might even pay a little extra. That way, the Robin Hood will feel at ease, and his trust in me will likely grow a little. After all, his work ultimately helps me make a profit, so in the long run, it’s a win-win.
“My son is under your care… How about this much?”
“You’re sure this won’t put you in a bind, right? Also, we’ll discuss the next matter after I’ve seen the chocolate from your place.”
“Yes. I’m prepared for that.”

Perhaps the tension had eased for her as well, because she stood her ground without backing down an inch. It’s this tense atmosphere that keeps business going, I suppose. I left the Robin Hood’s house and was shown the blocks of chocolate stored in the warehouse.
She handed me a piece as if it were a sample, so I put it in my mouth. The flavor and smoothness weren’t bad… in fact, they were quite good. Even a connoisseur would rate it as high quality.
“Does your company not partner with any other merchants? If necessary, I can talk to them as well.”

Just as I nudged her, the Robin Hood’s mother looked away. To be honest, that’s what’s bothering me. The quality is good and the price is reasonable, yet no one is buying it—it would be strange not to suspect there’s something fishy going on.
“It’s not that there aren’t any… but…”
Just as we were talking, the sound of an explosion echoed through the area. The Robin Hood’s mother pressed her hand to her forehead and groaned.
“Ah… Just when our business talks were going so well.”
“What? Is that a problem?”
“Well…”
“Our chocolate isn’t bad! Please, don’t stop the negotiations!”

The Robin Hood’s younger sister pleaded, clinging to me as if begging for mercy. Am I some kind of monster?! I can’t do anything without knowing the circumstances! Why am I being treated like a debt collector who’s come to collect?
“Come to think of it, your son—and those chocolate farmers I spoke to on my way here—all said to only talk to your mother and sister.”

In a typical family, that would mean the father is absent. Or maybe a younger brother? I wondered where he was or if there was some kind of problem… As I was thinking that, I noticed smoke rising from what looked like a workshop—the source of the deafening noise.
“Man, I messed up, I really did. I thought I’d finally get it right this time, though.”

With that, a slightly plump middle-aged man in a white lab coat emerged from the workshop. A vague sense of foreboding hung in the air. It was the same feeling I’d had when I first met Melty and when I’d spoken with the previous heroes.
“Hm? Who’s that? Who’s the one who dared set foot on my property?!”

I get a really bad vibe from him. It’s not just the way he says “I,” but also that self-assured way he talks. I can safely assume he’s the one causing all this trouble. That Robin Hood-type ran away from home, and even the villagers have caught on to what’s going on. In my opinion, he’s definitely the same kind of Trash as those before him.
“Dad! The Shield Hero came here with a letter of introduction from my brother! If he buys some chocolate, we can fix up our leaning house!”
So that’s what this business meeting was all about!? Even I have to admit that’s a bold claim… but is this farmhouse really that crooked?
“I don’t know anything about that guy!”

When my sister showed my father the letter of introduction from the Robin Hood I’d brought, he went and ripped it to shreds! I don’t mean to defend the Robin Hood, but this is starting to piss me off.
“What are you doing! We’re barely keeping this place afloat on my brother’s allowance and the Hero’s aid!”
“Shut up!”

Then the father slapped the Robin Hood’s sister across the face and glared at his wife. I’m totally grossed out by the domestic violence unfolding right before my eyes. Is this some kind of drama or something? Even in another world, a scene like this is rare. …Wait, maybe it’s not that rare. I’ve seen the queen do that to some Trash before. Though in that case, she had a good reason to do it.
Still, that Robin Hood guy—is he sending money from his own pocket on top of my aid? Somehow… it’s not like I’m giving him a raise, but I found myself thinking I should bump up his cut a bit.
“How dare you try to sell my chocolate without my permission!”
“You! Stop chasing dreams and face reality already!”
“Hmph! The world will recognize my invention any minute now!”
Just from this conversation alone, I can tell what a Trash this guy is. Anyway, that idiot dad needs to be punished.
“You called me a fake Shield, didn’t you? If you want my chocolate—”
“Someone’s an imposter! Raphtalia, shut this guy up!”
“Let’s talk before resorting to violence…”
“Alright! Then you!”
“Guaaaaaa!”
Strike first to win—I point at Chick and signal her to land the finishing blow on the idiot. Chick kicks the guy who looks like the Robin Hood-type dad.
“Guaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
With a satisfying thud, Chick’s kick sinks into the “Robin Hood” dad’s stomach, sending him flying. Looks like she went easy on him, though.
“Kyaaaaaahahaha! Dad!”
“You! Hahaha!”
What are you guys laughing at, pretending to be surprised? You’re such heartless bunch! Hey! Well, I already know what you’re really thinking from that exchange. Try to hide it a little better!
Spinning round and round, the “Robin Hood” dad fell into what looked like a swamp covered in chocolate.
